Does this meet:
> Substantial use may be demonstrated via use in many projects, or in one or a few significant projects.
?

License text, from https://lists.debian.org/debian-legal/2009/01/msg00118.html -- since that appears to be a source with plain text that doesn't have encoding artifacts. I haven't yet run a comparison to ensure this matches the version at https://artlibre.org/licence/lal/en/, but I will.

This license appears to have been around since at least 2009, and possibly longer; appears to have been drafted sometime between 2006-2009. See [discussion at debian-legal](https://lists.debian.org/debian-legal/2009/01/msg00118.html). Was also discussed [on debian-legal again in 2011](https://lists.debian.org/debian-legal/2011/01/msg00042.html), and debian-legal appears to call it ["status is unsettled"](https://wiki.debian.org/DFSGLicenses#Licence_Art_Libre_.28Free_Art_License.29) for DFSG purposes.

However, Open Knowledge calls it ["conformant" with the Open Knowledge Definition](https://opendefinition.org/licenses/) -- which makes it sufficient for [Other Factor 1 of the License Inclusion Principles](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/blob/main/DOCS/license-inclusion-principles.md).

For a couple of the key remaining other factors:
* this is a general license that can be used by anybody
* the long history of the license being around and approved by Open Knowledge, as well the list of images at https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:FAL-1.3, to me indicate sufficiently substantial use

Given that, I'm +1 to add this as a new license, with `FAL-1.3` as the identifier and "Free Art License 1.3" as the full name.

**Comment**
I consent with @swinslow. +1 to add.

I'm a bit on the fence but I'm also wondering (per the statement in https://wiki.debian.org/DFSGLicenses#Licence_Art_Libre_.28Free_Art_License.29) if there are translation issues in this one that make the English-translation less than the actual scope.

I'm hanging up on this clause:  "You have the right to copy this work for yourself, your friends or
any other person, whatever the technique used."   This seems more restrictive/personal than a blanket right to copy which licenses like MIT/GPL provide.
Discussed in meeting, OK to add given adoption by Open Knowledge Foundation.
`FAL-1.3` as the identifier and "Free Art License 1.3" as the full name
